Hi Sam — thanks, this is super helpful. Below is a succinct set of definitions and a couple of pricing scenarios so you can see invoice-level math. Jordan / Ben, please feel free to adjust numbers before I push to the term sheet PDF.

Definitions (how Redwood surfaces and charges bursts):
- Sustained quota: baseline soft quota we provision for a customer (monthly tokens at the agreed baseline unit price).
- Burst window: short timeframe where throughput exceeds sustained quota and is eligible for burst pricing. Default burst windows are two-fold: a short window (60s) for microbursts and a rolling 1-hour window for sustained spikes. Billing uses a rolling-window peak model to avoid charging for single short spikes.
- Quota increase: a manual or pre-approved temporary uplift to sustained quota. Requests submitted via Console/API are processed automatically if they match pre-approved thresholds; otherwise they go to a 2-business-day review by our Capacity Ops team.
- Overage billing: any consumption beyond sustained quota (and beyond any approved temporary uplift) is billed at the overage rate for the month. We calculate overage on consumed tokens above baseline after any applied credits/allowances.

Sample pricing scenarios (example math shown for clarity):
Scenario A — Baseline-friendly (target economics)
- Baseline: 150M tokens/mo at $800 per 1M tokens = $120,000/mo.
- Peak campaign: two 3-day campaigns with average 3x daily traffic on campaign days. Assume net consumption for month ends at 180M tokens. Overage = 30M tokens -> Overage rate applied at $1,200 per 1M = $36,000 incremental.

Scenario B — Burst allowance + capped overage (preferred for marketing teams)
- Baseline: 150M tokens/mo at $820 per 1M (slightly higher commitment rate) = $123,000/mo.
- Burst allowance: auto-allow bursts up to additional 25M tokens/month at $1,000 per 1M.
- Any consumption beyond baseline + burst allowance billed at $1,400 per 1M. If month hits 200M tokens, the math = baseline 150M @ $820 + 25M @ $1,000 + 25M @ $1,400 = $123,000 + $25,000 + $35,000 = $183,000.

Operational guardrails we recommend:
- Pre-approved campaign windows: we can whitelist campaign dates to allow automated temporary quota increases (instant, up to pre-set limit).
- Auto-throttle fallback: for unsolicited sustained spikes (no pre-approval), prefer auto-throttle to a smaller model variant and send an alert to your SREs — prevents runaway spend.
- Spend cap notifications + soft cutoffs: Console alerts at 70/85/95% of monthly committed spend and optional hard cut at 120% unless manual override.

Attachments: I attached a short term-sheet template and a two-tab spreadsheet with scenario math (redwood-overage-term-sheet.pdf, quota-scenarios-090226.xlsx). Jordan will follow with the draft overage clause language for procurement.
